messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: high queue backlog detected for tenant AcmeCorp on dedicated-pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42. queue_length=482, p95_latency=1.25s, error_rate=3.4%. Paging @sara (oncall) and @james-rt. Runbook: dedicated-tenant-bulk-queue.
sara (oncall): taking it. I'm SSHing to the scheduler master to pull metrics. tagging @pete-cs so CS is aware. anyone see recent deploys to that pool? :eyes:
james-rt: no deploys in last 2 hours. seeing a big tail of very large requests from AcmeCorp (some single requests with > 80k tokens). They look like batched eval runs hitting the reserved capacity. stack traces show lots of schedule_waits.
maria-ml: that matches what I saw in model telemetry — KV cache churn + huge batch token counts. For dedicated pools we usually cap per-tenant max_batch_tokens but looks like AcmeCorp has an override in place (unbounded) from an older onboarding patch.
sara (oncall): ok immediate mitigation options? we need to reduce customer impact quickly without taking entire pool offline.
james-rt: plan A: create a per-tenant scheduler override to force smaller batches and limit concurrency. Plan B: move the tenant to a lower-priority dedicated slice (isolated) while we tune. Plan C: apply per-tenant rate-limiting if they can't reconfigure upstream.
ben-night: I'm available to do the isolate and config patch. suggest this short-term override patch:
```yaml
tenant_overrides:
  acmecorp:
    scheduler:
      max_batch_tokens: 512    # cap largest batch size
      max_batch_time_ms: 35    # faster flush to avoid tail
      max_concurrent_requests: 3
    rate_limit:
      requests_per_second: 25
``` 
This keeps latency stable and still allows throughput. Will have downstream cost impact.
pete-cs: I alerted AcmeCorp support lead (J. Lee). They say they are running nightly heavy scoring jobs but can throttle if we ask — asked them to pause non-critical evals for 30m.
sara (oncall): apply the override as emergency change. @ops-bot please create a short-lived canary route to move AcmeCorp to dedicated-slice-iso-07 and apply the override there. keep existing pool in read-only for telemetry.
ops-bot: acknowledged. Creating route and applying config. Running dry-run then apply. ETA ~4m. (automated: change-id=chg-2026-1769456789-01)
incident-bot: Pager update: mitigation in progress. Post-mitigation check scheduled at +10m. Please update with customer impact notes.
maria-ml: note on knob rationale: lowering max_batch_tokens prevents a single request from monopolizing the batch scheduler and reducing KV cache thrash. max_batch_time_ms tradeoff: flush faster reduces batching efficiency but drastically lowers p95.
james-rt: after patch we should also add a defensive sentinel in scheduler: if queue_length_per_tenant > 200 then temporarily enforce rate_limit 10r/s and scale down batch window. I'll open a follow-up RFC for a permanent per-tenant graceful-degradation policy.
ben-night: ops-bot reports applied. Moving traffic to iso slice now. Early telemetry shows queue_length down to 120 and p95 down to 420ms. error_rate dropping.
sara (oncall): handing off to ben-night for the 02:00-06:00 window. I'll stay on standby until CS confirms customer acceptance. ben, please own the postmortem and link the incident ticket.
ben-night: ack. created INC-3421 and a postmortem stub. will include timeline, config diff, and customer remediation steps. link: https://go/reports/INC-3421 (internal)
pete-cs: customer confirmed they paused the heavy job and saw immediate improvement. They asked for a permanent cap recommendation — we should propose a production-friendly max_batch_tokens and a per-tenant throttle plan.
maria-ml: for long-term, recommend default tenant max_batch_tokens=1024 for enterprise but require opt-in for >1024 with explicit SLAs. also add a scheduler heuristic to detect KV-churning workloads and suggest cache pinning.
sara (oncall): notes for handoff: 1) mitigation applied (isolation + override), 2) customer paused heavy job, 3) follow-ups: postmortem (INC-3421), RFC for per-tenant graceful degradation, config cleanup removing the old unbounded override, and a CS docs update on best-practices for large scoring jobs.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: acmecorp high backlog mitigated. Closing pager. If latency rises again, will re-open. :white_check_mark:
ben-night: leaving final runbook comments and the exact patch diff in INC-3421. TL;DR of the emergency patch included above. Will schedule a full remediation tomorrow AM with Maria and James.
sara (oncall): thanks team. reaction :thumbsup:. closing thread.
